_portal: portal.html RENDERS THIS FILE, so recording a reading against it changes the page the reading was taken from. Readings are taken on the build immediately before the entry is written; chasing the fixed point would not terminate, and what differs between the two builds is table text, altering no rule the three gates apply. KNOWN GAP: portal.html is a pageTarget of those gates but is NOT in their `inputs`, so editing it does not age its own cells. That is deliberate and it is a compromise. `inputs` is per GATE, not per cell -- kitchen-sink.html already ages the templates' cells -- so adding a page regenerated on every verify would mark every browser cell stale on every build, including cells it has nothing to do with. The narrower fix is per-cell inputs, which is a redesign of the registry and a separate decision.
_visual: LOOKED AT, 2026-08-29 at 0d10eaa, viewport 1671x1048 in a widened pane -- the first time this sweep opened the pages rather than only measuring them. All 34 sink sections and all six templates, both the rendered page and, where a specimen is stateful, its states driven by hand. IT FOUND ONE DEFECT, AND NO GATE COULD HAVE. The table sort arrow was built from i-arrow--down, but Carbon’s glyph is ArrowUp and --descending rotates it 180deg, so both states pointed the wrong way. Nothing reads which symbol a <use> targets. CLEARED ON INSPECTION, each checked rather than assumed: the menu--with-icons specimen is visibility:hidden at rest because it is the TRIGGERED menu and opens correctly on click, not a repeat of the four hidden specimens this project shipped; the dropdown column that appeared to draw its list over its own trigger is the labelled list-box--up variant; the batch bar moves aria-hidden and tabindex together across select and deselect; every other hidden element resolved to a closed modal, a collapsed accordion, a hover tooltip, an empty search’s close button, or an unselected tile’s checkmark. G100 PASS, same day, same viewport, theme asserted from the resolved token (--rux-field-hover #333333, body rgb(22,22,22)). All 34 sink sections and all six templates again. ZERO DEFECTS. The inversions that carry real risk were each looked at rather than assumed: the inline high-contrast notifications go white-on-dark while the low-contrast ones stay dark with a coloured rule, which is the correct swap; the High contrast tag becomes a white pill with dark text; the modal overlay is rgba(0,0,0,0.6) over a rgb(38,38,38) surface with focus on the close button and the X still pinned top-right; the sort arrow still reads up for ascending. ONE OBSERVATION THAT IS NOT A DEFECT AND SHOULD NOT BE FIXED. Theming a template’s CONTENT to g100 makes the side nav merge into the page: nav, header and body all resolve to rgb(22,22,22) and nothing draws a divider. That is Carbon’s own definition -- @carbon/styles gives .side-nav background-color: $background and no border -- and it is not the state the templates ship, which is a g100 shell over white content, where the boundary is plain. Recorded so the next reader does not "fix" a faithful compile.
